definitions.explanation: Decisively proceeding with a plan despite obstacles or concerns.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}を{決行|けっこう}する。

examples.english: Will be held rain or shine.

examples.japanese: {強行|きょうこう}{決行|けっこう}
{反対|はんたい}の{声|こえ}があったにもかかわらず、{社長|しゃちょう}は{新|あたら}しいプロジェクトの{決行|けっこう}を{決|き}めた。
examples.english: Despite voices of opposition, the president decided to go ahead with the new project.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}が{近|ちか}づいていたが、{登山|とざん}を{決行|けっこう}した{結果|けっか}、{遭難|そうなん}しかけた。
examples.english: Despite the approaching typhoon, they went ahead with the mountain climb and nearly got stranded.

notes:
{決行|けっこう} means to carry out or go ahead with something decisively, often despite difficulties or concerns.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {雨天|うてん}{決行|けっこう}: rain or shine (event will proceed regardless)
- {計画|けいかく}を{決行|けっこう}する: to carry out a plan
- {強行|きょうこう}{決行|けっこう}: to force through; push ahead despite opposition
- {決行|けっこう}{日|び}: the day of execution

NUANCE:
Implies determination and resolve. Often used when proceeding despite obstacles, risks, or opposition.

HOMOPHONE:
Different from {結構|けっこう} (quite, fine, enough, no thank you) - same reading but different kanji and meaning.
